articles.title: Chasing The Mongolian Eclipse
articles.summary: Ernie Pini recounts his experience chasing the March 9, 1997 solar eclipse in Mongolia with a large group, overcoming initial cloud cover and a unique 'eclipse tax.' Despite an early morning, five-hour journey from Ulan Batar to an observation site near Darhan, the group was driven by the prospect of witnessing the eclipse alongside comet Hale-Bopp.

articles.title: Activities Calendar
articles.summary: This activities calendar outlines upcoming astronomical events and club engagements for May and June. It features numerous public star parties at locations like Houge Park and Fremont Peak, details general club meetings with guest speakers, and highlights educational opportunities such as beginning astronomy classes and major conferences.

articles.title: Yosemite National Park Star Party
articles.summary: The SJAA is organizing a star party at Yosemite National Park on June 27-28, which, while offering short nights and moon presence, provides a significant benefit by including a reservation at Bridewell Creek Campground and free park access amidst current restrictions. Attendees can enjoy Yosemite's active falls and should contact Jim Van Nuland to arrange registration and paperwork.

articles.title: School Star Parties
articles.summary: The school star party program is recessed for the remainder of the season, with May being impractical for grade schools due to late sunsets. The author extends thanks to all participants, whose contributions were greatly appreciated, noting favorable comments from teachers and their interest in future events.

articles.title: Jay Freeman
articles.summary: This article discusses the ongoing debate regarding the comparative performance of refractors and reflectors for observing lunar and planetary fine detail. While many observers believe refractors offer superior views for their aperture, the author suggests a 3:2 equivalent aperture ratio based on personal experience. However, a specific side-by-side test revealed a larger 8-inch Dobsonian reflector significantly outperformed a 90mm Vixen fluorite refractor in resolving intricate lunar details like the Alpine Valley rille.

articles.title: Richard Stanton
articles.summary: This document presents an astronomical ephemeris for May 1997, detailing celestial events and planetary positions over the month. It provides extensive data including rise, transit, and set times, magnitudes, and distances for the Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. The ephemeris also covers lunar phases, astronomical twilight times, sidereal time, and a highlighted 'Darkest Saturday Night' date.

articles.title: Eclipse, continued from page 1
articles.summary: This article recounts a challenging expedition to observe a total solar eclipse in Mongolia, marked by an aggressive bus driver, treacherous road conditions, and unexpected snow. Despite logistical setbacks like a delayed breakfast and thick clouds, the observers raced against time to find a narrow clearing just minutes before totality. They successfully witnessed the eclipse, enduring extreme cold and technical preparations, ultimately deeming the overall journey, including cultural visits, a rewarding experience despite the less-than-perfect viewing conditions.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: The document serves as a periodical publication statement for the "SJAA Ephemeris," the monthly newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association. It specifies that the newsletter is published 12 times a year, from January through December, and provides the association's address. A publication date of May 1997 is also referenced.

articles.title: SJAA Observing Sites
articles.summary: The article outlines various observing site possibilities for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), categorized by distance from town, ranging from in-town options for bright objects to more distant dark sky locations. It discusses specific locations like Fremont Peak and Henry Coe, while also encouraging member input and assistance for site development and potential projects like Amateur Telescope Making (ATM). The goal is to galvanize further ideas and actions to support the club's observing and project needs.

articles.title: Directions to SJAA places
articles.summary: This document provides detailed driving directions to several parks: Houge Park, Henry Coe State Park, Fremont Peak State Park, and Grant Ranch County Park. These locations are associated with the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) or other local astronomical groups for events like star parties. The directions include specific turns, distances, and notes on entrance fees for some parks.

articles.title: Figures Supplied By Treasurer Bob Elsberry
articles.summary: Treasurer Bob Elsberry has provided a series of financial reports for the San Jose Astronomical Association, including a recent balance sheet and reports for Q1 1997 and Full Year 1996. These documents confirm the association's strong financial health, showcasing substantial resources in both its checking account and Observatory Fund.

articles.title: SJAAMC Balance Sheet - Actual
articles.summary: This document presents the actual balance sheet for SJAAMC as of March 29, 1997. It details total assets, which include a checking account and two savings funds (Gregory Fund and Observatory Fund), amounting to $11,389. The organization had no liabilities, with all assets corresponding to its General Fund equity.

articles.title: SJAAMC Income and Expenses - Actual vs. Budget
articles.summary: This document provides a financial overview for SJAAMC, detailing actual income and expenses against budgeted figures for the period of January 1 through March 29, 1997. The organization saw significantly higher actual income than budgeted, mainly from dues receipts and book sales. However, total expenses also exceeded the budget, largely due to increased costs for ephemeris and subscriptions, resulting in a net positive financial variance for the period.

articles.title: SJAAMC Income and Expenses – Total and By Quarter (January 1 through December 31, 1996)
articles.summary: This document presents the detailed income and expenses for SJAAMC for the full year 1996, broken down by quarter. It itemizes various income sources such as dues, donations, and auction proceeds, alongside expenses including subscriptions, Ephemeris publication, and organizational dues. The report concludes with a total net income of $2019.72 for the year, despite an initial loss in the first quarter.

articles.title: Don Machholz
articles.summary: This article provides updates on prominent comets, detailing Comet Hale-Bopp's diminishing visibility for Northern Hemisphere observers and the recovery of Periodic Comet Tempel-Tuttle, responsible for the Leonid meteor shower. It also introduces "Comet Comments," a monthly column by Don Machholz, which offers new comet discoveries, news, observing tips, and ephemerides for amateur astronomers. The column also explains how to interpret astronomical data like Right Ascension, Declination, Elongation, and Magnitude for comet observation.

articles.title: Ephemerides - Epoch 2000, 0h UTC
articles.summary: This document provides ephemerides for three comets—C/1995 O1 (Hale-Bopp), 81P/Wild 2, and 46P/Wirtanen—for the period covering early May through mid-June 2000. The tabulated data, specified at Epoch 2000, 0h UTC, includes their Right Ascension, Declination, Elongation (EL Sky), and apparent magnitude to aid in their observation.

articles.title: Orbital Elements - Epoch 2000.0
articles.summary: This document provides a tabular listing of orbital elements for three comets: Hale-Bopp, P/Wirtanen, and P/Wild 2, all referenced to Epoch 2000.0. The data includes details such as perihelion date and distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, and orbital period, along with their respective MPC references. This information appears to be part of an ephemeris for May 1997.

articles.title: Astro Ads
articles.summary: This document features 'Astro Ads' for used astronomical equipment, including a Meade LX200 10-inch telescope, a Celestron C90 spotting scope, and a Celestron Firstscope 60 EQ, complete with accessories and contact information for sellers. It also provides guidelines for submitting free non-commercial ads and articles to the SJAA Ephemeris newsletter.

articles.title: Lassen Star Party Closed
articles.summary: Sign-ups for the Lassen star party, scheduled for the Fourth of July weekend, are now closed. All available spaces for the event have been filled.

articles.title: Mike Koop
articles.summary: This document, titled "Mike Koop," appears to be a list of astronomical telescopes available for loan to members of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). It details various telescopes, their current borrowers, and due dates, along with a waiting list and contact information for reserving equipment. One specific note seeks information about a borrower who never returned a 6" f9 Dobsonian telescope.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the officers and Board of Directors, including their positions, names, and phone numbers. It also identifies the Ephemeris Staff members responsible for editing, printing, and mailing, along with the Mentoring Program Chairman. The article serves as a directory for key personnel within the organization.

articles.title: Activities Committee
articles.summary: This document lists the chairpersons and contact information for various committees and programs within an astronomy organization, likely SJAA, as of May 1997. It includes contacts for the Activities Committee, Observational Astronomy Teacher, Observatory Committee, School Star Party, Telescope Loaner Program, and Web Page.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is the membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing membership fees for new and renewing members ($15) and juniors ($6). It also offers an optional Sky & Telescope magazine subscription for an additional $27. Members are instructed to make checks payable to "SJAA" and submit the form and payment either at a meeting or by mail to the Treasurer.
